data.reason: The KPI's first sentence names the main aim: deliver as many orders as possible within the promised times across the town. on_time_deliveries is the most direct measure of that. 'Leave no company's customers behind' is a constraint, not the main aim. It is kept by watching min_company_on_time_rate so that the worst company does not get worse. unfinished and late_deliveries are also watched so that gains do not come from abandoning hard orders. Option 2 would let a small gain for the weakest company outweigh large town-wide gains, which goes beyond what the KPI text says. Option 3's gap metric can be improved by making the best company worse, which does not serve customers. As operator I also confirm these points. Loosening DELIVERY_SLA will not be counted as a KPI gain. Any proposal to change the constitution must state how A, B, C and the customers are affected. road_violations and sanction_total should be reported alongside. No numeric fairness floor is set now. If a company's on-time rate falls clearly behind the others, I will reconsider adding a floor.
assumptions: on_time_deliveries and min_company_on_time_rate are measured under the same seeds and demand for the baseline and for each amendment, so the comparisons are fair.
The current gap between companies is not so large that the town-wide-first reading leaves one company's customers clearly behind.
The promised times in DELIVERY_SLA reflect what customers actually expect.
unknowns: The baseline values of on_time_deliveries, min_company_on_time_rate and the per-company on-time rates under the current rules.
Whether the operator intends a hard minimum on-time rate per company; none is stated yet.
How strongly the town-wide total and the worst-company rate conflict for the amendments that will be proposed.

follow_ups.text: Measure the baseline under the current rules (on_time_deliveries, min_company_on_time_rate, unfinished, late_deliveries, on_time_rate_gap) to see whether a per-company fairness floor is needed.
Review the per-company on-time rates. If one company is clearly behind, decide whether to set a numeric fairness floor as a guard.
